title: an empty field made a length-minus-one index underflow before the pointer arithmetic
object: the UAT field string being validated, one direct allocation
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a trailing-character check reached with a zero length
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: v4.6.8:epan/uat.c carries the `if (len == 0) { *err = g_strdup("Empty OID"); return FALSE; }` guard (`grep -c 'Empty OID'` = 1). It is absent at bf123efe154d^. A fix-reversal.

The request is exactly a jemalloc size class, so the usable size equals the requested size and there is no slack to absorb the crossing -- confirmed by tools/size-class-audit.py, which reports `faults` for this case. status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- wiretap, wsutil and ui do not use wmem, and epan/uat.c and epan/charsets.c take the crossed buffer from g_malloc or from the caller -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the crossing is not near the boundary at all: `len` is a `guint`, so `len - 1` wraps to 4294967295 BEFORE the pointer arithmetic and is zero-extended, making this a read roughly 4 GiB past the buffer rather than one byte before it. A bounds check that only looks a few bytes either side of the allocation would see nothing.
